validity.recommendation: No action beyond the two spec notes below. Existence, classification, duplicate-check, ownership and location all check out on independent, currently-live sources.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguously real, and about as concretely confirmed as a pipeline can be — the actual PIPELINE-CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTOR's own project page (proyectosdelgolfo.com, a South Texas/Mexico pipeline builder) describes 'Gasoducto Nueva Era pipeline spread 2' in construction-scope detail: trenching, 30-inch pipe stringing/welding/coating, right-of-way clearing, from south Texas to the municipio of Escobedo, Nuevo Leon, rated up to 600 MMcf/d. That is a primary construction record, not press coverage. Independently: Howard Midstream Energy Partners LP's SEC Form S-1/A (filed as amended 2017-11-21, CIK 1690884, accession 0001193125-17-349673 — fetched directly with a compliant SEC User-Agent header since sec.gov 403s the verifier's default UA/bot-wall; NOT included in proposed_refs for that reason, same as the Oasis Pipeline P0234 precedent) states in its own combined financial statements: 'HEP and CLISA both hold a 50% membership interest in NEP, a joint venture to construct and operate a 200-mile natural gas transportation pipeline that will transport natural gas supplies from the U.S. to end-users in and around Monterrey, Mexico' and gives audited financial statements for 'Nueva Era Pipeline, LLC and Affiliates' as a real operating entity with real revenue/EBITDA. Natural Gas Intel (naturalgasintel.com, trade press, live and verified), El Financiero (elfinanciero.com.mx, two separate live articles: the 2018-06-13 in-service piece and an earlier 2018-01-16 '80% built' construction-progress piece), and Grupo Clisa's own current corporate site (grupoclisa.com.mx) all independently corroborate the same physical, in-service asset. S&P Global Platts' 2018-07-02 headline ('Nueva Era pipeline system begins commercial service, boosting US-to-Mexico gas supplies') and a San Antonio Business Journal 2018-06-06 piece on final testing exist and are on-topic per their gem.wiki citation text, but both are access-blocked today (Platts 403, bizjournals behind a Cloudflare/Incapsula challenge that also blocks the Wayback crawler — confirmed via a fresh Wayback capture that itself serves the block page) — access failures, not deletions, so not cited but not treated as concerning either given the other five working sources. This is not remotely a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a gas transmission trunk (not gathering/gathering-adjacent) — every source describes it as a long-haul, cross-border natural gas transportation pipeline moving South Texas production to CFE combined-cycle power plants and industrial users in the Monterrey metro area; Fuel=Gas is correct (no NGL/liquids ambiguity anywhere in the record). DUPLICATE: checked against all 44 other rows in the 45-row roster. No other row shares this corridor or footprint — the nearest candidate, P0215 Mier Monterrey Gas Pipeline (Starr County -> Nuevo Leon, 90 mi), is a geographically and physically distinct crossing (different Texas county of origin, roughly half the length, no shared ownership); no other row touches Nuevo Leon or a Webb County origin. No merge/relabel indicated. ATTRIBUTION/OWNERSHIP: Owner1=Howard Energy Partners 50% / Owner2=Grupo Clisa 50% matches the SEC filing's explicit 'HEP and CLISA both hold a 50% membership interest in NEP' exactly (uncitable per the rule above, but decisive), and is independently consistent with Grupo Clisa's own site describing the project as 'Surge de una sociedad entre Howard Midstream Energy Partners y GRUPO CLISA' (a partnership between Howard Midstream Energy Partners and Grupo Clisa) and Natural Gas Intel calling it 'a joint venture between HEP and Mexico's Grupo Clisa' — see the Owner fill below for the citable-tier caveat on the exact 50/50 split. Operator='Nueva Era Pipeline LLC' matches Natural Gas Intel's own phrasing verbatim ('the genesis of Nueva Era Pipeline LLC') and the SEC filing's legal-entity name 'Nueva Era Pipeline, LLC'. LOCATION: StartPrefecture/District=Webb County, Texas and EndLocation=Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico are directly confirmed by El Financiero's June 2018 article ('El ducto transportara gas natural desde el condado de Webb, Texas hasta Monterrey') and by the January 2018 El Financiero piece, which additionally names the more granular Mexican-side receipt/delivery points (a receipt point at the community of Colombia, Nuevo Leon, near the border, with delivery to CFE's Monterrey II/III combined-cycle plants in Pesqueria and to El Carmen) — all within the greater Monterrey area GEM's EndLocation already reflects, so no change needed, just a more granular routing note for a future route-creation pass. Also noted for the record (not actioned, not one of this row's owed value cells): the January 2018 El Financiero piece calls the project 'tambien conocido como Laredo-Nuevo Leon' (also known as 'Laredo-Nuevo Leon') — a candidate OtherEnglishNames alias, flagged for Update rather than added here. COVERAGE: of the 19 harvested wiki citations for this page, I opened/attempted 11: naturalgasintel.com (read, live), elfinanciero.com.mx/monterrey (read, live), elfinanciero.com.mx/economia (read, live), grupoclisa.com.mx (read, live), proyectosdelgolfo.com (read, live), eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (read, live but a generic boilerplate landing page — not itself an existence signal), fractracker.org (live, not read in depth — a generic map-tool announcement page, low marginal value), rbnenergy.com (403, and its Wayback lookup hit archive.org's rate limit), bizjournals.com (Cloudflare/Incapsula-blocked, confirmed via a live fetch and via a Wayback capture that itself serves the block page), spglobal.com/platts (403), howardenergypartners.com/growth and the HEP open-season PDF (both genuine 404s — Howard Energy Partners restructured its site; these are confirmed dead, not merely blocked). Not opened: ijglobal.com's three listings (a subscription paywall serving only a lead-gen page to anonymous fetches — confirmed by inspecting the raw HTML, which is a Gravity Forms login/marketing shell with no article content; not citable even if it loads 200), the TxDOT PDF (a generic statewide freight-corridor study, unlikely to carry pipeline-specific specs), and the Bloomberg 2021 Texas gas-export-ban piece (about a different, later regulatory episode, not this pipeline's core facts).

validity.researcher_notes: DIAMETER: Natural Gas Intel and the proyectosdelgolfo.com construction-contractor page both independently and explicitly describe 30-inch pipe (the mainline). The '36' component of GEM's 'Diameter = 30, 36' is confirmed verbatim by Howard Midstream Energy Partners' SEC Form S-1/A: 'The Nueva Era pipeline comprises approximately 19 miles of 36-inch pipeline and approximately 181 miles of 30-inch pipeline' (19+181=200 mi, exactly matching LengthKnown too) — but sec.gov 403s the verifier's UA (confirmed with a compliant SEC header out-of-band), so per standing practice it is not in proposed_refs. No source contradicts a 36-inch segment existing; it simply isn't independently citable at 36-inch specificity beyond that one filing, so I'm not treating this as a real spec concern, just noting the citation-tier gap. LENGTH: LengthKnown=200.00 mi (321.9 km) is the SEC filing's own headline figure ('an approximately 200-mile natural gas pipeline from Webb County, Texas to the Monterrey, Mexico area', repeated twice) and is consistent with IJGlobal's project-finance transaction titled 'Nueva Era Gas Pipeline (318.6KM) Refinancing 2018' (=197.9 mi — IJGlobal's own listing pages are paywalled/lead-gen shells with no readable body text, confirmed by inspecting the raw HTML, so not citable, but the title string itself, harvested from gem.wiki, is a second independent data point). The CITABLE press/promotional sources instead describe an approximate, slightly lower figure: Grupo Clisa's own page says 'longitud aproximada de 300 kilometros' and El Financiero's June 2018 piece implies a similar ~300 km total (27 km Texas-side + 275 km Mexico-side per company spokesperson quotes to Natural Gas Intel, repeated in Spanish); but El Financiero's earlier January 2018 construction-progress piece instead describes 'mas de 300 kilometros de construccion en ambos paises' (MORE than 300 km) — an open lower bound fully consistent with 321.9 km, not a contradiction. Net read: this is a single family of consistent figures reported at different rounding precision (a round '~300 km' marketing/interview figure vs. a precise 200.0-mi/318.6-321.9-km regulatory-filing/project-finance figure), not a material spec disagreement worth a value change.

validity.researcher_notes: SegmentCost [ref]: no source states a $500,000,000 cost for the Nueva Era Pipeline, and the one specific project-financing figure I did find is materially lower. IJGlobal's transaction record (Transaction ID 35133, 'Nueva Era Gas Pipeline', last updated 15/12/2016; Wayback capture http://web.archive.org/web/20210801100037/https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/35133/nueva-era-gas-pipeline, since the live page is paywalled) states in its free summary: 'The $353.4 million proceeds will be used for the development of the Nueva Era natural gas pipeline, a 321 km of minimum 30-inch (76 cm) pipeline that extends from Howard's Webb County Hub in South Texas, United States, to Escobedo in Nuevo Leon and to the Mexican...' -- i.e. a dated, transaction-specific financing figure of $353.4 million for this pipeline's development, not $500 million. I'm not proposing this as a REFS_ADDED source for the sheet's $500M value (it contradicts it), and I'm not treating it as fully dispositive either, since IJGlobal describes it as loan/note 'proceeds' for a specific financing round rather than an unambiguous statement of total all-in project cost (there could be additional equity or other capital outside this note). I checked whether other sources corroborate either figure: Howard Midstream Partners LP's SEC Form S-1/A (2017, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690884/000119312517349673/d287008ds1a.htm) shows a balance-sheet line 'Construction in progress $125,440' (thousand, i.e. $125.44 million) as of December 31, 2016 -- a snapshot mid-construction, consistent in magnitude with a low-$100s-million-to-mid-$300s-million total rather than $500 million, but it does not itself state a total project cost figure, so I'm not citing it as a second source for the same $353.4M claim. Two related IJGlobal transaction records for the same pipeline -- ID 40356 ('Nueva Era Gas Pipeline Additional Facility,' holdco financing for the same ~320km line) and ID 43402 ('Nueva Era Gas Pipeline (318.6KM) Refinancing 2018') -- exist but their dollar amounts are paywalled (only generic teaser text visible via Wayback, no figure). I did not find a $500 million figure anywhere, including in: Natural Gas Intel's HEP WahaRey/AguaRey pipelines article (fetched in full, 256,941 bytes -- describes capacity/diameter/CFE offtake, no cost figure); Howard Energy Partners' own August 2015 open-season press release (recovered via Wayback PDF, https://web.archive.org/web/20240810215532/https://www.howardenergypartners.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/NuevaEraCFEFinal-8.12.15.pdf, extracted with pdftotext -- no cost figure); Howard Energy Partners' company growth/timeline page (recovered via Wayback, https://web.archive.org/web/20231202154519/https://www.howardenergypartners.com/growth -- the only dollar figures on the entire page are unrelated 2022 corporate financing items, '$400 million of unsecured debt' and a '$1 billion revolving credit facility', which are general HEP corporate facilities, not a Nueva Era construction cost); two El Financiero Spanish-language articles (both fetched in full -- report capacity figures, no 'inversion'/cost figure found after multiple targeted searches); Grupo Clisa's own project page (has a generic 'INVERSIONES' section heading but no dollar figure); Proyectos del Golfo (capacity only); the TxDOT International Trade Corridor Plan (2023 PDF, https://ftp.dot.state.tx.us/pub/txdot/move-texas-freight/studies/international-corridor-plan.pdf, fetched and extracted with pdftotext -- describes Nueva Era's capacity/diameter/length and CFE anchor contract in detail, no cost figure). RBN Energy's seed URL (rbnenergy.com/node/11486) turns out to be a topic/tag index page titled 'Nueva Era | RBN Energy' (confirmed via both the live 403-blocked fetch and a Wayback capture), not an article -- a navigation surface, so not usable as a citation even where accessible. San Antonio Business Journal and S&P Global Platts seed URLs both returned blocked/paywalled responses (5,933 and 597 bytes respectively) with no Wayback snapshot available for either specific article path. WebSearch quota was exhausted for this session throughout, so I could not run open web searches for a possible EIA/trade-press restatement of $500 million; all of the above came from direct fetches, Wayback recovery, and PDF extraction. Net: the one dated, project-specific dollar figure that exists ($353.4 million, IJGlobal, Dec 2016) is well below the sheet's $500 million, so this is flagged as a likely sheet overstatement/data issue for Update rather than resolved as REFS_ADDED -- I have not changed the value or proposed a citation that would misrepresent it as supporting $500,000,000.

fills.researcher_notes: Both trade-press/local-press sources describe the pipeline ramping to commercial service in mid-2018 ('ramped up in May' / gas injection began June 13, 2018), corroborated by an S&P Global Platts headline confirming 'commercial service' July 2, 2018 (blocked by verifier today, not cited). No indication anywhere of a later shutdown, sale-and-idle, or decommissioning; a live 25-year CFE offtake contract from 2018 runs to ~2043, consistent with continued operation.
Both sources describe it explicitly as a natural gas transportation pipeline ('gas natural') supplying CFE combined-cycle power plants; no NGL/liquids ambiguity anywhere in the record.

El Financiero (dated 2018-06-13, gas injection begins) and Natural Gas Intel (mid-June 2018, 'ramped up in May', full service expected by month end) both place in-service in 2018, corroborated by an S&P Global Platts headline dated 2018-07-02 confirming 'begins commercial service' (blocked by verifier today, not cited) and by an earlier El Financiero piece (2018-01-16) forecasting a second-half-2018 start when construction was 80% complete.

Three independent origins agree on 600 MMcf/d design capacity: Natural Gas Intel ('designed to carry at least 600 MMcf/d and up to 1 Bcf/d'), the pipeline's own construction contractor ('hasta un maximo de 600 millones de pies cubicos por dia'), and El Financiero's construction-progress piece ('transportar alrededor de 600 millones de pies cubicos diarios ... con compresion, la capacidad podria incrementarse a unos 800 millones'). Do not confuse with the separate, smaller CFE-contracted anchor volume of 504 MMcf/d (also widely reported) — that is the offtake commitment, not the pipeline's design capacity; GEM's 600 MMcf/d correctly records the latter.

See the paired spec validity note: the precise 200-mi figure traces to Howard Midstream Energy Partners' SEC S-1/A (uncitable per verifier, sec.gov 403s its UA) and is consistent with IJGlobal's project-finance listing title '(318.6KM)' (197.9 mi; paywalled, not citable). The two citable Spanish-language sources given here corroborate an open-ended 'more than 300 km' / 'approximately 300 km' figure, which is compatible with but less precise than 321.9 km — tier set to medium rather than high to reflect that the exact 200.00 mi figure itself is not independently pinned down by a citable source, only bracketed/approximated by one.

The 30-inch component is directly and independently confirmed by Natural Gas Intel and by the pipeline's own construction contractor (which describes stringing/welding 30-inch pipe on 'spread 2'). The 36-inch component is confirmed only by Howard Midstream Energy Partners' SEC S-1/A ('approximately 19 miles of 36-inch pipeline and approximately 181 miles of 30-inch pipeline') — uncitable per verifier (sec.gov 403s its UA), so tier is set to medium rather than high to reflect that only one of the two diameters clears the independent-citable bar on its own; both numbers are corroborated, just not to the same citation standard.

El Financiero states directly: 'El ducto transportara gas natural desde el condado de Webb, Texas hasta Monterrey' (the pipeline will carry natural gas from Webb County, Texas to Monterrey). Natural Gas Intel independently corroborates the Webb-County-to-Monterrey routing and the CFE Monterrey-area offtake. A separate El Financiero piece (2018-01-16) gives finer Mexican-side granularity not currently in GEM's fields — a receipt point at the community of Colombia, Nuevo Leon near the border, delivering to CFE Monterrey II/III (Pesqueria) and El Carmen — flagged for a future route-creation pass, not actioned here since EndLocation=Monterrey already reasonably covers the metro area.

Could not independently verify the $500,000,000 figure. Howard Midstream Energy Partners' SEC S-1/A gives project-finance-adjacent dollar figures (e.g. a $138.1 million EFG-lease payment stream to the sponsor, and Nueva Era Pipeline LLC's own combined financial statements for 2016) but no single stated total construction/project cost matching $500M, and none of the citable press sources state a project cost figure at all. IJGlobal (ijglobal.com) lists what are almost certainly the underlying project-finance transactions (an original financing, a 2018 refinancing, and an 'additional facility') that would carry the authoritative cost/financing figures, but all three IJGlobal URLs harvested from the wiki page return only a subscription paywall/lead-gen shell to an anonymous fetch (confirmed by inspecting the raw HTML — a Gravity Forms marketing page, no article body), so the figure is not independently recoverable right now. Left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate or silently pass a guessed source; not treated as a concern since $500M is a plausible order-of-magnitude figure for a 200-mile, 600 MMcf/d international pipeline and nothing contradicts it.

Natural Gas Intel names the entity verbatim: 'the genesis of Nueva Era Pipeline LLC, a cross-border system ... a joint venture between HEP and Mexico's Grupo Clisa'. Howard Midstream Energy Partners' SEC S-1/A independently uses the identical legal name 'Nueva Era Pipeline, LLC' throughout its combined financial statements (uncitable per verifier, not counted toward the independence tally, but corroborating). [QC 2026-09-02: single-origin — `independent` reset to False per the confidence rubric (>=2 AGREEING independent sources), tier capped at medium.]

Grupo Clisa's own current site describes the project as 'una sociedad entre Howard Midstream Energy Partners y GRUPO CLISA' and Natural Gas Intel independently calls it 'a joint venture between HEP and Mexico's Grupo Clisa' — both confirm the two-owner joint-venture STRUCTURE and identity. Neither citable source states the exact percentage split; the precise 50.00%/50.00% figure traces to Howard Midstream Energy Partners' SEC S-1/A ('HEP and CLISA both hold a 50% membership interest in NEP') which 403s the verifier's UA and is therefore not in proposed_refs. Tier set to medium to reflect that the ownership identity is high-confidence/independent but the exact split rests on one uncitable regulatory filing.
